mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,300k units triggers a negative demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1300 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of sustained high unemployment (>4.5% for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based supply-side shock, which historically precedes negative equity returns as profit expectations deteriorate over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent drop in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% signals a deflationary easing cycle, which historically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower real borrowing costs and improved corporate margins.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 2.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such deflationary easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 400k new jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and increases cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month change > 400k for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during such periods of rapid payroll acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500k units month-over-month combined with a concurrent rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend by more than 1.5% signals a recovery in demand, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month +500k AND GDPC1 > trend +1.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such demand recovery signals.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1.5% for four consecutive months signals a robust supply-side expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings expectations improve.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month change > 1.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained industrial production acceleration.
